global_silver_linings.snippet: A ten-year-old plant has finally burst into flower for the first time after a decade of care by professional horticulturists—and the stalk was so tall greenhouse had to remove the Roof. Staff at the Birmingham Botanical Gardens even needed to open the roof after the towering flower spike shot up to more than 18 feet […] The post Plant’s First Flower is a ‘Death Bloom’ So Tall the Greenhouse Had to Remove Ceiling Panels appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: A plant patiently growing for years before producing a flower so magnificent it literally outgrew its ceiling is a reminder that nature operates on its own magnificent scale, indifferent to our limits. There's something quietly wonderful about humans having to make way for a living thing to fulfill its purpose.

discovery_articles.title: Reynard’s Cave in England
discovery_articles.snippet: Hidden in a section of limestone above Dovedale lies Reynard's Cave. The small cave is situated behind a large natural rock arch and the combination is one of the Peak District's most distinctive geoligical features. Excavations in the late 1950s suggested that the cave was used as a spot of temporary refuge during the Neolithic, Roman and Medieval periods.

discovery_articles.title: Torthorwald Castle in Torthorwald, Scotland
discovery_articles.snippet: The first castle at this location was a simple earthwork motte-and-bailey construction, built at some point in the 12th century. The site of Torthorwald Castle was owned by David Torthorwald by the 13th century. During the First War of Scottish Independence, some of Sir David's descendants supported the English army.

garden_note.note: Late summer lingers in the Zürich air tonight, the linden blossoms long finished but the kitchen garden pressing on with quiet abundance — courgettes still swelling, tomatoes finally blushing on the vine. Step out after supper into the last warmth of the day; the garden exhales something almost autumnal after dark.
